newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Flughafen sees more incentive payments.
newsitem.headline: Flughafen sees more incentive payments.

text.p: Austrian airport operator Flughafen Wien said on Thursday incentive payments and tarriff cuts for its airline customers had cost 170 million schillings in 1996 and were likely to cost a similar amount this year.

"Incentives and reductions together have totalled about 170 million schillings," chief executive Franz Kotrba told the group's annual earnings conference, adding that incentive payments were expected to reach a similar level this year.

Flughafen earlier on Thursday reported an 11 percent drop in 1996 net profit to 602 million schillings, blaming the decline on payments to its customers which it said had been necessary to preserve the group's long-term earnings potential.

Flughafen has been under mounting pressure to cut its ground handling costs -- among the highest in Europe -- as an increasing number of airlines has threatened to set up their own ground handling operations to cut down on costs. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
